paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God keeps His promises, and He makes a way to save His people. The LORD told Moses the last plague was coming, and He said He would make a distinction between Egypt and Israel (Exodus 11:7). The blood on the doorframe was that sign, and the LORD said, "when I see the blood, I will pass over you" (Exodus 12:13). Israel was spared because they trusted what He said and did just what He commanded, not because they were better than anybody.

Now look at what the LORD asked for. A lamb, unblemished, and the blood on the doorframe. Then they stayed inside until morning (Exodus 12:22). I think that's a lot to ask of a family with their sandals already on, and the people still did it. I think that's what trust looks like, friend: you do what He says, even when the night is long and the door is the only thing between you and the unknown.

And then the LORD says, "this day will be a memorial for you" (Exodus 12:14). He told them to remember it, and to tell their children what it meant (Exodus 12:26-27). That's for you too, baker. When God saves, you don't just say thanks and move on, you REMEMBER, and you pass it down. I still remember the day the Most High reached into that drawer and pulled me out, and I will tell that story until my ovens go cold.
